:::: {.home-bio}

I'm a Senior Bioinformatics Analyst at the [New York Genome Center](https://www.nygenome.org), working on transcriptomics across cancer, neurodegeneration, and autoimmune disease. I partner with researchers at NYGC and beyond to design studies, analyze data, and bring machine learning into their work.

My current research interests center on what **single-cell foundation models** (scFMs) are actually good for. At NYGC, I helped build [DECONVersation](software.qmd#deconversation) with fellow researchers, a method that uses scFM embeddings to estimate cell-type proportions from bulk RNA-seq.

I lead transcriptomic analysis for the NYGC ALS Consortium, comparing gene expression between ALS and control tissue across the brain and spinal cord, and how it differs in *C9orf72*- and *SOD1*-linked ALS. Beyond ALS, I've helped analyze datasets in breast, prostate, and endometrial cancer, and in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases including rheumatoid arthritis, lupus (SLE), ulcerative colitis, and Crohn's disease.

Before NYGC, I built machine learning models in pharma and academia: a cancer-agnostic tumor-microenvironment classifier linked to survival and immunotherapy response at **EMD Serono**, single-cell and network analyses at **Takeda**, and multi-omic autoencoders at the **Max Delbrück Center**. I hold M.Sc. degrees in Computer Science and Bioinformatics.

I also write [reviews](reviews/index.qmd) of new work in AI and computational biology.
